([[The Bronx|The Bronx, New York]]) | college = * [[Minnesota Golden Gophers men's basketball|Minnesota]] (2017–2019) * [[Iona Gaels men's basketball|Iona]] (2019–2020) * [[Long Beach State Beach men's basketball|Long Beach State]] (2020–2021) | draft_year = 2021 | career_start = 2021 | career_end = | years1 = 2021–2022 | team1 = [[KK Lovćen 1947|Lovćen 1947]] | years2 = 2022–2023 | team2 = [[Spišskí Rytieri]] | years3 = 2023 | team3 = [[Skyliners Frankfurt]] | years4 = 2023–2024 | team4 = [[Würzburg Baskets]] | years5 = 2024–2025 | team5 = [[SLUC Nancy Basket]] | years6 = 2025 | team6 = [[Antonine University|CS Antonine]] | years7 = 2025–2026 | team7 = [[BC Nizhny Novgorod|Nizhny Novgorod]] | years8 = 2026 | team8 = [[Basket Zaragoza|Zaragoza]] | highlights = * [[Mr. New York Basketball]] (2017) }} '''Isaiah Washington''' (born July 20, 1998) is an American professional [[basketball]] player who last played for [[Basket Zaragoza]] of the [[Liga ACB]]. He played for [[St. Raymond High School for Boys]] in [[The Bronx]], where he was named [[Mr. New York Basketball]] in 2017. Washington co-founded and popularized Jelly Fam, a [[social media]] movement that emphasizes creative [[finger roll]] layups. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Minnesota Golden Gophers men's basketball|Minnesota Golden Gophers]], [[Iona Gaels men's basketball|Iona Gaels]], and [[Long Beach State Beach men's basketball|Long Beach State]]. ==Early life== Washington was born and raised in [[Harlem]], a neighborhood in the [[New York City]] borough of [[Manhattan]]. He grew up playing basketball at Dunlevy Milbank Children's Center in Harlem.{{cite web |last1=Cordova |first1=David |title=Isaiah Washington: Lord of the Jelly; Minnesota-Bound PG Leaves Lasting Impact on High School Basketball |url=https://davesjoint.net/2017/04/26/isaiah-washington-lord-of-the-jelly-minnesota-bound-pg-leaves-lasting-impact-on-high-school-basketball/ |website=Dave's Joint |accessdate=February 14, 2020 |date=April 26, 2017}} In junior high school, Washington and his friend, Ja'Quaye James, along with [[Jahvon Quinerly]], began calling themselves "Jelly Fam."{{cite web |last1=Danois |first1=Alejandro |title=Jelly Fam: Welcome to the New Hoops Phenomenon |url=https://thelab.bleacherreport.com/jelly-fam-new-york-city-basketball-isaiah-washington/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161130123216/http://thelab.bleacherreport.com/jelly-fam-new-york-city-basketball-isaiah-washington/ |url-status=dead |archive-date=November 30, 2016 |publisher=[[Bleacher Report]] |accessdate=February 14, 2020 |date=November 28, 2016}}{{cite web |last1=Jordan |first1=Jason |title=Elite PGs Jahvon Quinerly and Ja'Quaye James primed to take Jelly Fam movement to next level |url=http://usatodayhss.com/2017/jahvon-quinerly-jaquaye-james-jelly-fam-movement |publisher=USA Today High School Sports |accessdate=June 19, 2018 |date=June 13, 2017}} The phrase became popular among basketball players through social media and was centered around fancy [[finger roll]] layups called "jelly."{{cite web |last1=O'Donnell |first1=Ricky |title=How a New York City high schooler made 'the jelly' the coolest move in basketball |url=https://www.sbnation.com/college-basketball/2017/11/7/16487372/jelly-layup-finger-roll-isaiah-washington-jelly-fam-explainer |publisher=[[SB Nation]] |accessdate=February 14, 2020 |date=November 7, 2017}}{{cite web |last1=Fuller |first1=Marcus |title=Isaiah Washington, with Jelly Fam brand in tow, gives Gophers basketball a recruit like none other |url=http://www.startribune.com/isaiah-washington-with-jelly-fam-brand-in-tow-gives-gophers-basketball-a-recruit-like-none-other/436072533/ |website=[[Star Tribune]] |accessdate=February 14, 2020 |date=July 24, 2017}} Washington trademarked the name. ==High school career== Washington played basketball for [[St. Raymond High School for Boys]] in [[The Bronx]], a borough of [[New York City]].{{cite web |last1=Braziller |first1=Zach |title=Why next great high school point guard is staying in NYC |url=https://nypost.com/2016/08/27/why-next-great-high-school-point-guard-is-staying-in-nyc/ |website=[[New York Post]] |accessdate=February 9, 2020 |date=August 27, 2016}} On August 26, he shared [[most valuable player]] (MVP) honors at the Elite 24 All-American Game after scoring 36 points.{{cite web |last1=Calle |first1=Franklyn |title=2016 Under Armour Elite 24 Recap |url=https://www.slamonline.com/college-hs/2016-armour-elite-24-recap/ |website=[[Slam (magazine)|Slam]] |accessdate=February 9, 2020 |date=August 22, 2016}} As a senior, he averaged 26 points and six assists per game. Washington scored a season-high 54 points in a 91–83 loss to [[Cardinal Hayes High School]].{{cite web |last1=Jorge |first1=Leo |title=Cardinal Hayes Survives Isaiah Washington's 54-Point Performance |url=https://www.madehoops.com/news_article/show/753489-cardinal-hayes-survives-isaiah-washington-s-54-point-performance |publisher=MadeHoops |accessdate=February 9, 2020 |date=February 5, 2017}} He finished his career as St. Raymond's all-time leading scorer with 1,410 points, surpassing [[Darryl Bryant]], and was named [[Mr. New York Basketball]], becoming the fourth point guard to ever win the award.{{cite web |last1=Fuller |first1=Marcus |title=Gophers recruit Isaiah Washington named Mr. Basketball New York |url=http://www.startribune.com/gophers-recruit-isaiah-washington-named-mr-basketball-new-york/416642723/ |website=[[Star Tribune]] |accessdate=February 9, 2020 |date=March 20, 2017}} ===Recruiting=== Washington was a consensus four-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and the highest rated New York point guard in the 2017 class. He committed to play [[college basketball]] for [[Minnesota Golden Gophers men's basketball|Minnesota]] over offers from several other [[NCAA Division I]] programs.{{cite web |title=NYC Guard Isaiah Washington Commits to Minnesota |url=https://www.slamonline.com/archives/nyc-guard-isaiah-washington-commits-minnesota/ |website=[[Slam (magazine)|Slam]] |accessdate=February 9, 2020 |date=September 12, 2016}} {{College athlete recruit start|40=no|collapse=no|year=2017}} {{College Athlete Recruit Entry | recruit = Isaiah Washington | position = [[Point guard|PG]] | hometown = [[Harlem|Harlem, NY]] | highschool = [[St. Raymond High School for Boys|St. Raymond]] (NY) | feet = 6 | inches = 1 | weight = 160 | 40 = | commitdate = September 11, 2016 | scout stars = | rivals stars = 4 | 247 stars = 4 | espn stars = 4 | espn grade = 85 }} {{College Athlete Recruit End | 40 = | year = 2017 | rivals ref title = Minnesota 2017 Basketball Commitments | 247 ref title = | espn ref title = 2017 Minnesota Golden Gophers Recruiting Class | rivals school = minnesota | 247 school = | espn schoolid = 135 | rivals overall = 62 | 247 overall = 65 | espn overall = 68 | accessdate = June 18, 2020 | bball = yes }} ==College career== On November 10, 2017, Washington made his collegiate debut, recording four points and five assists on 1-of-9 shooting for Minnesota in a 92–77 victory over [[USC Upstate Spartans men's basketball|USC Upstate]].{{cite web |title=Murphy, No. 15 Minnesota Overpower SC Upstate |url=https://gophersports.com/news/2017/11/10/Murphy_No_15_Minnesota_Overpower_SC_Upstate.aspx |website=University of Minnesota Athletics |publisher=[[Associated Press]] |accessdate=February 20, 2020 |date=November 10, 2017}} On February 3, 2018, he scored a career-high 26 points in a 76–73 overtime loss to [[Michigan Wolverines men's basketball|Michigan]]. It was the highest-scoring performance by a Minnesota freshman in [[Big Ten Conference]] play since [[Kris Humphries]] in 2004. He was subsequently named Big Ten freshman of the week.{{cite web |last1=Fuller |first1=Marcus |title=Gophers' Isaiah Washington named Big Ten freshman of the week |url=http://www.startribune.com/gophers-isaiah-washington-named-big-ten-freshman-of-the-week/472786483/ |website=[[Star Tribune]] |accessdate=February 20, 2020 |date=February 5, 2018}} As a freshman, Washington played 32 games and averaged 8.7 points, 2.6 rebounds and 2.3 assists per game, shooting 36.6 percent from the field.{{cite web |last1=Jungheim |first1=Nick |title=The game is beginning to slow down for Isaiah Washington |url=https://www.mndaily.com/article/2019/02/s-the-game-is-beginning-to-slow-down-for-isaiah-washington |website=[[Minnesota Daily]] |accessdate=February 20, 2020 |date=February 6, 2019 |archive-date=February 21, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200221035156/https://www.mndaily.com/article/2019/02/s-the-game-is-beginning-to-slow-down-for-isaiah-washington |url-status=dead }} On December 11, 2018, during his sophomore season, he posted his first [[double (basketball)|double-double]], with 14 points and a career-high 13 assists in an 80–71 win over [[North Florida Ospreys men's basketball|North Florida]]. Washington averaged 4.3 points and 2.8 assists on 31.1 percent shooting as a sophomore and received less playing time due to the emergence of Gabe Kalscheur.{{cite web |last1=Fuller |first1=Marcus |title='Jelly' Isaiah Washington is jelling on floor for Gophers |url=http://www.startribune.com/jelly-isaiah-washington-is-jelling-on-floor-for-gophers/503670022/ |website=[[Star Tribune]] |accessdate=February 20, 2020 |date=December 30, 2018}}{{cite web |last1=Fuller |first1=Marcus |title=Jelly finds a new home: ex-Gophers PG Isaiah Washington transfers to Iona |url=http://www.startribune.com/jelly-finds-a-new-home-ex-gophers-pg-isaiah-washington-transfers-to-iona/510000452/ |website=[[Star Tribune]] |accessdate=February 20, 2020 |date=May 16, 2019}} For his junior season, he transferred to [[Iona Gaels men's basketball|Iona]], moving closer to his hometown of Harlem to spend time with his ailing grandmother, and was granted immediate eligibility by the NCAA.{{cite web |last1=Thomson |first1=Josh |title=NCAA says Iona's Isaiah Washington is eligible to play this season |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/college/iona/2019/10/23/ncaa-grants-ionas-isaiah-washington-transfer-waiver/4070484002/ |website=[[USA Today]] |accessdate=February 20, 2020 |date=October 23, 2019}} In his first eight games, Washington averaged 7.8 points per game and shot 28 percent on three-pointers, but he grew more comfortable with his teammates and improved his statistics as the season progressed. On January 26, 2020, he tallied 25 points and 10 rebounds in a 94–88 loss to [[Monmouth Hawks men's basketball|Monmouth]].{{cite web |last1=Rapay |first1=Eugene |title=Despite team's struggles, Iona's Isaiah Washington showing improvement |url=https://www.lohud.com/story/sports/college/iona/2020/02/06/iona-college-basketball-isaiah-washington-jelly-fam-showing-improvement/4669861002/ |website=[[The Journal News]] |accessdate=February 20, 2020 |date=February 6, 2020}} On February 27, Washington posted the third [[triple-double]] in Iona history with 14 points, 11 assists, and 10 rebounds in an 86–65 win over [[Canisius Golden Griffins men's basketball|Canisius]].{{cite news |title=Washington's triple-double leads Iona over Canisius 86–65 |url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/washingtons-triple-double-leads-iona-over-canisius-86–65/ |accessdate=April 3, 2020 |work=[[CBS Sports]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=February 27, 2020}} Washington averaged 11.4 points, 5.1 rebounds, and 4.0 assists per game.{{cite news |last1=Hancock |first1=Jacob |title=Rick Pitino is back in college basketball after scandal forced him out; Twitter reacts to his return |url=https://www.sportingnews.com/us/ncaa-basketball/news/rick-pitino-back-college-basketball-twitter-reacts-return-hall-of-fame-coach-scandal/ag480nx1fk751wvzs9v05jn5k |accessdate=April 3, 2020 |work=[[Sporting News]] |date=March 14, 2020}} On May 21, 2020, he entered the transfer portal as part of a mutual agreement with new head coach [[Rick Pitino]] and his staff.{{cite web |last1=Rapay |first1=Eugene |title=College basketball: Iona's Isaiah Washington enters name into transfer portal |url=https://www.lohud.com/story/sports/college/iona/2020/05/21/college-basketball-isaiah-washington-transfer-out-iona/5239953002/ |website=[[The Journal News]] |accessdate=May 21, 2020 |date=May 21, 2020}} On June 15, 2020, Washington announced that he was transferring to [[Long Beach State Beach men's basketball|Long Beach State]].{{cite web |last1=Polacheck |first1=Jacob |title=Long Beach State lands Iona transfer Isaiah Washington |url=https://www.zagsblog.com/2020/06/15/long-beach-state-lands-iona-transfer-isaiah-washington/ |publisher=Zagsblog |accessdate=June 15, 2020 |date=June 15, 2020}} As a senior, he averaged 13.7 points and 4.9 rebounds per game.{{cite news |title=UCSB faces Long Beach St. in Big West quarters |url=https://apnews.com/article/isaiah-washington-uc-santa-barbara-gauchos-mens-basketball-chance-hunter-santa-barbara-mens-college-basketball-26eaab0a0f1749adaf773a500e39a79b |access-date=June 20, 2021 |work=[[Associated Press]] |date=March 10, 2021}} ==Professional career== After going undrafted in the [[2021 NBA draft]], Washington signed with [[KK Lovćen 1947|Lovćen 1947]] of the [[ABA League Second Division]] and the [[Prva A Liga]].{{cite web |last1=Markovic |first1=Rado |title=Druga Liga Round 1: Lovcen rally past Pelister |url=https://www.eurobasket.com/ABA-League/news/709342/Druga-Liga-Round-1:-Lovcen-rally-past-Pelister |website=Eurobasket |access-date=March 9, 2022 |date=October 14, 2021}} On August 12, 2022, Washington signed with [[Spišskí Rytieri]] of the [[Slovak Basketball League]].{{cite web |last1=Búza |first1=Oliver |title=Prichádza Americká Polisa Isaiah Washington |url=https://www.basketsnv.sk/prichadza-americka-posila-isaiah-washington/ |website=Basketball in SNV |access-date=December 18, 2022 |date=August 12, 2022}} On January 8, 2023, Washington signed with [[Skyliners Frankfurt]] of the [[Basketball Bundesliga]].{{cite web |last1=Nawrath |first1=Thomas |title=FRAPORT SKYLINERS VERPFLICHTEN POINT GUARD ISAIAH WASHINGTON |url=https://www.fraport-skyliners.de/news-service/details/fraport-skyliners-verpflichten-point-guard-isaiah-washington/ |website=Fraport Skyliners |access-date=January 10, 2023 |date=January 8, 2023}} On June 8, 2024, he signed with [[SLUC Nancy Basket]] of the [[LNB Pro A]].{{Cite web|url=https://sluc-basket.fr/actualites-du-club/isaiah-washington-prend-la-mene.html|title=Isaiah Washington prend la mène|last=|first=|date=June 8, 2024|website=sluc-basket.fr|publisher=|language=fr|access-date=June 10, 2024}} In 2025, Washington played for [[Antonine University|CS Antonine]] of the [[Lebanese Basketball League]] and [[BC Nizhny Novgorod|Nizhny Novgorod]] of the [[VTB United League]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.eurobasket.com/VTB-United-League/news/944532/Isaiah-Washington-ex-Antonine-is-a-newcomer-at-NNovgorod|title=Isaiah Washington (ex Antonine) is a newcomer at N.Novgorod|last=|first=|date=July 21, 2025|website=eurobasket.com |publisher=|language=en|access-date=January 27, 2026}} On January 27, 2026, Washington signed with [[Basket Zaragoza]] of the [[Liga ACB]] and [[EuroCup Basketball|EuroCup]].{{Cite web|url=https://acb.com/articulo/ver/546277-isaiah-washington-refuerza-la-direccion-de-casademont-zaragoza.html|title=Isaiah Washington refuerza la dirección de Casademont Zaragoza|last=|first=|date=January 27, 2026 |website=acb.com |publisher=|language=es|access-date=January 27, 2026}} Zaragoza announced it was parting ways with Washington on May 18, 2026.{{Cite web|url=https://www.casademontzaragoza.es/noticias/isaiah-washington-no-continuar%C3%A1-en-casademont-zaragoza|title=Isaiah Washington no continuará en Casademont
